fix(onchain): unpin the retired 36-byte out-ref key from the InputSets machine phase (#592)

Landed while #592's rebind was measured indivisible and re-homed to
#593 for rulings: the InputSets phase pinned the retired 36-byte
out-ref key at two sites (encode_input_sets_scan_witness's domain
assertion and input_sets_control_is_bound) while verify_input_sets_item
reads previous_key off the §5.3 item it decodes - 38 bytes since #586 -
so the phase crashed inside its own witness encoder on any step that
had read one input. Both sites now name
native_tx_field_access_v1.spend_input_item_bytes; the two affected
baseline rows move from "program failed" aborts to a clean False on the
counted conjunct, so all 22 owned rows now fail for exactly the one
#592 cause. Plus the countedMachineFieldTraceV1 docstring gains the
measured both-halves size and the #593 pointer.

Verification: fork-runner full check 1686 / 22 failed, byte-identical
by name to #585's baseline; isolated stock builds (v1.1.22+39d6b04,
env -u MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN) show exactly 4 changed entries / 2 named
validators (input_sets_empty_semantic_v1, input_sets_item_semantic_v1)
- recorded on #592 for #579's applied-hash cascade; in-tree plutus.json
byte-identical (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); exec ledgers pass
without --update (no measured row exercises InputSets); stock-fmt CI
sim idempotent on the edited .ak; tsc/prettier clean;
validation-machine source-text suites 11/11.

#592 remains open: the rebind is one indivisible unit (15 sites, 8
phases, one TransactionFieldChunkWitness constructor) blocked on #593's
two rulings (which §8 tiers a machine step may name - tier-1's 14,336 B
bound vs the 16,225 B measured maximum field-2 preimage inside erratum
E1's window - and how an ungrammatical committed preimage is rejected
rather than aborted under the §4 door).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(core,sdk,validation,lucid,node,watcher): the nine-field consumer swap onto flat commitments (#585)

The flat-reversion centerpiece: the counted scheme dies TypeScript-side.
The first attempt (#578's measurement) was reverse-applied as
worse-than-either-end; this landing follows the three blockers it
surfaced - #586 (ledger out-ref unification), #587 (receipt chain
retirement), #588 (producer machinery) - so the swap ships as one
coherent unit.

midgard-core: all nine field derivations in native-body.ts /
native-witness.ts move to midgardFieldCommitmentV1 over §5.1 preimage
bytes; validateMidgardNativeTxCanonicalV1 is the §5.1 fail-closed
grammar walk at the encoder, canonical decoder and materialisation;
native-field-items.ts deleted (§5.1 collapses its three-way split);
verifyMidgardV1TxFieldPreimage flat; the counted per-item publication
surface (deriveMidgardV1TxFieldChunks/Evidence, verify chunk/item,
reconstruct-from-chunks, both evidence types) deleted; fields 5/6/8
into the §5.1 envelope; sortMidgardMintItemsV1 gives §5.6's two-level
sort one spelling; the §5.3 hash-28 and address-witness item encoders
are now the producers' format authority for fields 3/4/7.

Producers and consumers move together: lucid-midgard (mint -> §5.6
items, enveloped redeemers, one §5.1 byte-list encoder), midgard-
validation ledger-tx codec + redeemers (retired dual-spelling decode
gone), sdk EMPTY_SPEND_INPUTS_HASH eb25ed4a -> 45b0cfc2 =
blake2b_256(#"80") with the gap assertion flipped to convergence, four
sdk fraud-proof commitment helpers, fault-proofs hashSpendInputCbors +
transition-trace detect, node ingestion (reconstructMidgardTransaction-
V1 binding moved with the swap), and the node test fixtures that still
hand-built counted shapes (79/79, 20/20, 20/20 after migration to the
production encoders; transaction-root-v1 golden regenerated from its
producer, rf031 Aiken rows 10/10). The machine's remaining counted
trace in validation-machine.ts is fenced and documented as
self-referential (never compared to a §4 field hash in TS), owned by
#592.

Every cross-language vector regenerated from producers - never by hand:
the #588 generator chains, a fourth producing suite added to the
boundary generator (blob-chunk-boundary-v1 now publishes on the write
channel; its max-inline-datum Aiken twin had silently pinned retired
counted commitments and stayed green because counted-vs-counted is
self-consistent - exactly the divergence class this program repairs),
and the da-hash-preimage validator pair re-derived from the same
channel.

Fork-runner full check, by name: 30 -> 22. The ten #585 acceptance rows
go green (six native_tx_v1 C20/n02-n09 rows, high-cardinality /
size-balanced / ordinary-golden decodes, the max-redeemers terminal
commitment, and the one-step decode row). Two terminal-fold rows arrive
red: verify_canonical_decode_chunk checks a counted Merkle opening
against transaction_field_commitment() - §4 flat since #567 -
unsatisfiable by construction once TypeScript stops declaring counted
roots. That is mask-removal, not new breakage: the same machine-rebind
family as the 20 accepted validation_machine_v1 rows. Recorded as
Deviation 2 on the issue; owned by #592 (blocked_by #585, blocking
#579 - it lands before the single blueprint regeneration).

Verification: producer --check gates all green and failable; exec
ledgers pass without --update (no measured row moved; stock builds of
both trees byte-identical - aiken v1.1.22+39d6b04, env -u
MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN, md5 329cfe5697afc95984762a1b13273a84 - proving no
compiled-code change); stock-fmt CI sim zero drift on all ten touched
.ak; suites core 505/505, lucid 179/179, validation 269/271, sdk
235/236, da-committee 274, watcher 616/617 (timeout flake class),
fault-proofs 327/343 (16 rows all frozen-blueprint/applied-hash
classes, byte-identical across rounds), node repaired files green with
residuals only in the documented #579-owned classes. plutus.json
byte-identical (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); no parent-only
surface touched. Two review rounds + two fix rounds (63 masked node
failures repaired; 2 majors - both stale-green cross-language mirrors -
re-mirrored through producers; 12 minors fixed), then a CLEAN
confirmation pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(core,sdk,validation,lucid): producers for every hand-mirrored fixture seed family (#588)

Executes the 2026-08-10 owner ruling: write all generators first, no
hand-transcription exemptions, so #585's AC3 (ten named Aiken tests
green) and AC5 (vectors regenerate from producers, never hand-edited)
become jointly satisfiable. The point of this ticket is the machinery -
families whose TypeScript side moves in #585 regenerate again there.

New producers and seeds:
- native-size-balanced: the opaque 15.5k fullTxCborHex blob (no producer
  anywhere in the repo) is replaced by a declared construction -
  SIZE_BALANCED_PARAMETERS builds the transaction from stated
  parameters, emitting §5.3 38-byte out-refs; the old blob is gone from
  the tree and the fixture identity moved with the capability corpus
  row re-derived through its sanctioned --update gate.
- native-ordinary: golden_core_native_full_tx_cbor (the hand-maintained
  near-miss seed) gains a producer, so the ordinaryAikenPath branch has
  no hand-maintained seed left.
- native-high-cardinality: #586's sync writer verified against the
  ruling (idempotent, referenced).
- generate-native-tx-vector-v1-goldens.mjs (midgard-core): the n02-n09
  exact-vector family, emitted from the TS tests that compute them.
- generate-ordered-collection-boundary-aiken-goldens.mjs
  (midgard-validation) + aiken-vector-channel.ts: the C20-6, C20-7 and
  max-redeemers boundary-constant families.
- golden-channel.mjs gains name-keyed rebindAikenConstants (output must
  survive stock aiken fmt - CI's authority; the fork formatter is what
  agents must not run) and distinguishes missing constants from
  unrecognized literal forms; generate-native-compact-aiken-goldens.mjs
  rewritten with a freshness gate that re-derives every consumed facet
  (preimages, sizes, mint order, redeemer pointers) from fullTxCborHex,
  proven failable per facet class.

Evidence the machinery equals the transcription: first-run zero-value
diffs for n02-n09 and max-redeemers; the C20-6/C20-7 family had four
silently-stale constants (canonical byte counts 16685->16687 and
16871->16873, the compact CBOR and the field-preimage-lengths CBOR -
field 0 goes 0x1827->0x1829, the +2 of #586's fixed-index out-ref) which
the generator corrected; two undeclared duplicate seeds closed. All six
generators idempotent (second run byte-identical), all --check modes
clean and proven failable, each .ak module banners its seed/writer/
rebinder, each fixture JSON names its producer, two new CI gates invoke
the checks. docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §9 records the standard, scoped to
the named families with the terminal-fold structures tracked by #590
(new, blocked_by #588, does not block the trunk; its body carries the
per-site publish-channel inventory - four of six terminal-fold suites
need write channels first).

Verification: fork-runner full check 1686 / 30 failed, identical BY NAME
to #587's baseline - the predicted greening of the two size-balanced
rows does not happen because both carry second causes owned by #585
(counted mint map, counted commitments), recorded on the issue; CI fmt
pipeline (stock v1.1.22) zero drift on all touched .ak; exec ledgers
pass without --update (note: verifiers must run under
MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN=<fork> - bare PATH measures stock and reports sub-ppm
cpu drift); suites lucid-midgard 179/179, core 505/505, validation
269/271 (baseline), sdk 235/236 (baseline), da-committee 274/274;
plutus.json byte-identical (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); no
parent-only surface touched. Two review rounds (1 blocker - an
89-column line that stock fmt reflows, breaking CI's diff gate - plus 4
majors + 6 minors, all fixed; round 2 CLEAN).

refactor(onchain,sdk,node,watcher): retire the counted publication receipt chain (#587)

Executes the 2026-08-10 owner ruling: the tx-field receipt chain dies
before #579's single blueprint regeneration rather than being frozen
into it.

On-chain: validators/user-events/tx-field-receipt-v1.ak, its spend twin,
tx-field-preimage-v1.ak and lib/midgard/user-events/tx-field-receipt-v1
are deleted; ledger-state.ak loses TxFieldReceiptV1, TxFieldPreimageV1
and TxOrderPayloadV1.terminal_receipt_reference; tx-order-v1.ak sheds
every counted helper (receipt asset name, chain-link walk,
verify_order_receipts, both burn authorizers) for verify_order_material,
and the mint drops two parameters. The retired path was unsatisfiable on
two independent grounds for any payload whose commitments are the §4
flat hashes of real material - the docstrings state the declaring-
payload residual precisely, and verify_order_material's all-nine-empty
clause closes it by construction. The fragment-envelope fixture,
generator and gate go with it (make target replaced by
carriage-exec-ledger-v1, a gate for a gate).

Off-chain: SDK twins retired; new deriveTxOrderMaterialV1 plans carriage
per non-empty field through planMidgardFieldCarriageV1; the node's
ingestion walk and the watcher's forced-payload check lose the counted
reconstruction arithmetic ([0,1,2,3,4,7] byte-list branch, field-5 +-1
chunk offset). The ingestion walk deliberately stays on
reconstructMidgardTransactionV1 rather than the §8.8 door: against
#585's counted residual the door gate would compare the empty-field
constant to itself - a gate that cannot fail - and #589 owns the move.
The watcher's material-emptiness refusal is likewise not re-created: it
mirrored the retired mint walk exactly (a check no stronger than the
mint admits nothing new), and refusing at the observation gate was
measured to null every forced-inclusion verification block. Recorded on
the issue; #589 owns the availability-certificate check.

Deviation, recorded on #587 and re-homed to #589 (blocked_by 587, 579):
the §8.6 FieldPreimageCertificateV1 re-expression cannot ship from this
lane - the certificate validator is absent from the frozen blueprint and
all three deployment registries, and §8.4 routes preimages <= 14,336 B
to tier-1 redeemer carriage, which does not outlive its transaction.

Verification: fork-runner full check 1716/33 -> 1686/30, the delta being
exactly the three retired tx_order_v1 rows (their verify_order_material
replacements green); Q21 out-of-window row re-taken with cause note
(-7,324 mem / -2,307,365 cpu from the shed datum field), q1x/q31/
carriage unchanged, all verifiers pass without --update; suites at
accepted baseline across core 505, lucid-midgard 177, sdk 235/236,
validation 269/271, fault-proofs non-emulator 298/300, da-committee 274,
watcher 617/617, node targeted green; sdk-aiken-schema-parity moves 4->7
stale-blueprint rows (TxOrderPayloadV1Schema + two embedding schemas),
run-verified and recorded at both blueprint load sites (13-name handoff
set). Format registry L09/L10 become delete-disposition rows backed by a
new declaration-anchored absence scan; registry gate at its 1
pre-existing failure. plutus.json byte-identical
(c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5). Recorded for #579: abi-freeze
bound-gate counters, F05 manifest citations (12 defects incl. the
watcher 617 pin move), catalogue/registry validator rows, and
format-registry.md byte-pin bump. Two review rounds (4 majors + 8
minors, then 3 majors + 4 minors, all fixed or rebutted with measured
evidence).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(offchain,onchain): unify the ledger out-ref on the §5.3 fixed-index item encoding (#586)

Executes the 2026-08-10 owner ruling (erratum on #565): the ledger MPF
trie key is in the reversion's scope, and both consumers of the out-ref
bytes - the §5.3 field-0/1 items and the trie key / DB outref column -
move together onto the fixed-index 38-byte form
(82 || 58 20 tx_id || 19 index_be16). On-chain had derived the trie key
through this encoder since #567 while TypeScript still emitted CML's
minimal-index 36-byte form: a live cross-language divergence on the
fraud-proof replay path.

Producers/consumers migrated: lucid-midgard outRefToCbor/utxoOutRefCbor,
midgard-validation midgardOutRefToCbor/encodeOutRef +
validation-machine's ledger-trie insertion key and script-source bounded
item, midgard-node genesis/deposits/withdrawals/mpf + workload scripts,
sdk encodeMidgardTxInputCanonicalV1, core Cardano->Midgard conversion
(cmlInputsToSpendInputPreimageCbor), da-committee payload negative.
decodeMidgardOutRefBytes accepts exactly the §5.3 form - the CML
fallback chain and the retired canonical-cardano-fast-path decoder are
deleted, per the ruling's no-second-spelling rule; a stale dev ledger
resets, it does not migrate. The Aiken decoder gains the exact-38-byte
guard (decode_definite_bytes_at alone accepts a non-minimal 59 0020
header - one input, two trie keys), mirrored by negatives on both twins
and a golden-channel vector. The reference-script source key - also the
ledger out-ref - moves to the same encoder on both twins
(script-proof-v1.ak canonical_reference_source_key rewritten as a total
round-trip; the old minimal re-encode would have rejected every new key
with index < 256); recorded on #586 as a deviation from ruling item 5,
since script_proof_v1 compiles into four validators and the frozen
blueprint is now one step more stale for #579 to re-take together with
the applied-hash pins and necessity artifacts.

Spec: docs/spec/midgard-tx.md records the trie-key derivation as the
§5.3 field-0/1 item encoding, one spelling both languages. Fixtures
regenerated from producers only: cardano-capability corpus via its
--update gate, bench initial-ledger-state, native-high-cardinality (new
sync script), one-step cross-language fixture (producer migrated off
CML, --check mode added), transaction-root/transition-trace goldens, and
~110 hand-pinned constants re-captured mechanically with two-run
determinism checks. Stale-green Aiken twins re-mirrored through the
MIDGARD_PRINT_AIKEN_VECTOR channel, including the self-consistent
da-hash-preimage maximum pair.

Verification: cross-language golden_ledger_outref_key_matches_typescript
plus a 15-case TS twin (indices 0..65535 across the 23/24 boundary);
fork-runner full check 1716 tests / 33 failed - byte-identical by name
to the 34-name pre-#586 baseline minus
script_sources_replay_appends_reference_scripts, which this change
fixes; exec ledgers re-taken with cause notes (+1,312 mem / +358,482 cpu
once per execution that decodes an out-ref - identical at 1 and 296
inputs; growth readings unchanged) and all verifiers pass without
--update; suites green or accepted-baseline across core 506/506,
lucid-midgard 177/177, validation 269/271, sdk 237/238, fault-proofs
non-emulator 298/300, da-committee 274/274, watcher 614/616, node
targeted 428/428 and deposit-flow-emulator 14/14 serialized.
plutus.json byte-identical (c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5); no
parent-only surface touched. Three review rounds (1 blocker + 3 majors +
6 minors, then the ledger re-take, then clean).

refactor(onchain,sdk): single-anchor multi-field opening; retire committed-source transaction_commitment (#584)

Phase-5 follow-up, first of the two compiled-surface blockers ahead of
#579's single blueprint regeneration.

Single-anchor opening: field-opening-v1.ak gains an opaque
AnchoredNativeTxV1 handle (anchored_native_tx pays the tx-id derivation
and witness_set_hash check once) with anchored_field_view /
anchored_field_walk opening N fields against one anchor. Every opening
re-runs both guards - carriage_reaches_the_anchor and the §2.5
body/witness pairing - as separate expects so a refusal names its guard.
resolved_sources is deleted; opened_field_view/walk are thin wrappers, so
the guards have one spelling. The handle deliberately exposes no
witness_set_hash accessor (the #575 forgery class), and the validity-code
accessor is named unanchored_validity_code_of because that is what it is.
transition-trace's validate_l2_transaction_transition builds one handle
for its three body fields: Q21 L2 row 2,760,481 -> 2,334,205 mem (8%
under the 2,533,821 AC ceiling), forced-order row 3,034,025 -> 2,538,180.
Q31/Q1x single-field rows rose +7,117/+7,580 mem per opening (routing
through the handle + the guard split); re-measured, cause recorded in all
three exec ledgers, under 0.06% of the §3.3 basis.

Committed-source retirement: transaction_commitment leaves
L2TransactionSourceV1 and ForcedInclusionTxV1 (leaf value was always a
pure function of source; the L1 mint-time derivation check in
material_directory still pins TxOrderPayloadV1's copy, and
validation-claim-v1 re-anchors NormalValidationSource by deriving
source_proof_commitment directly - same value, same binding, one
derivation per claim as before). SDK twin and ~25 producer/reader sites
move in step; goldens regenerated on both language sides
(transaction-root-v1 fixture pair, transition-trace-abi.json,
ValidationSourceMembershipV1 corpus bf590321 -> 5cba4fd7, tx-order CBOR
vectors); format-registry arity pins 4 -> 3; tex/consensus-profile docs
updated. TxOrderPayloadV1 / TxFieldPreimageV1 / TxFieldReceiptV1 keep
their copies by design.

Verification: field_opening_v1 27/27 (three new second-open tier-guard
rows), transition-trace proof 38/38, full Aiken suite byte-identical 34
pre-existing failures vs HEAD, q21/q31/q1x/carriage exec-ledger
verifiers pass without --update, sdk-aiken-schema-parity 32/32 against a
scratch-built blueprint, TS suites green across sdk/node/watcher/
da-committee/fault-proofs. plutus.json untouched
(c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5): ten tests (six emulator, four
schema-parity rows) are red against the stale in-tree blueprint until
#579 regenerates it - the accepted price of the ordering, with the exact
set recorded at the blueprint load sites for #579's implementer.
Three review rounds (1 major + 9 minors, then 1 major + 5 minors, then
CLEAN); parent-only surfaces untouched.

docs(core,sdk): name the counted-scheme residual at the nine-field consumer call sites (#578)

Phase-5 lane D: the anticipated family-directory claim was empty - the
field-6 native-script family is Q17 missing-native-script-tx, which #575
took inside its Q10-Q19 block, and an audit of all sixteen directories
under validators/fraud-proofs/ (independently re-verified in review) found
no unclaimed directory left on counted-scheme access (Q20 min-fee already
reads through the door; Q44 da-hash-preimage frames the compact tx, not
per-field items; mpf-chunked-proof is clean).

Lane D therefore claimed the one surface the wave flagged repeatedly and
no lane took: the nine-field TypeScript consumer path. The flat swap was
attempted for real and measured - four lines changed, dists rebuilt,
every package diffed against its own baseline: 58 new failures across
four packages, rooted in two structural blockers (the counted per-item
publication receipt chain in consensus-validation-v1.ts with live
consumers in midgard-node/midgard-sdk, and the §5.3/§5.6 item grammar
never re-pointed in the TS producers). The swap was reverted as
worse-than-either-end and the work re-homed to #585, which now blocks
#579 via a native tracker edge (alongside #584, whose missing edge was
also recorded).

What lands in-tree is the honest residual: docstring annotations at
deriveNativeTxBodyCompact / deriveNativeTxWitnessSetCompact and the
zero-input fraud-proof builder naming the counted/flat gap at the call
sites, with one authoritative note (native-body.ts) and pointers from the
siblings, plus a durable test title asserting the counted-scheme empty
spend-inputs hash. Semantic inertness proven by AST comment-strip: three
files byte-identical after stripping, the fourth differs only in the
it() title.

#578's issue body carries a Deviation section with an AC-applicability
table: AC1 met (claim recorded, disjoint, audit confirmed), AC2 re-homed
to #585, AC3 provably N/A (no .ak change, no execution row owed), AC4
restated as no-regression (fork full check 1707/34 = HEAD's identical
failure set; the ten red Aiken tests are #585's exit criteria, pinned by
name there).

Verification: midgard-core 460/460; midgard-sdk 237/238 (single
pre-existing blueprint-drift failure owned by #579); tsc/eslint/prettier
clean; core+sdk dists rebuilt; stock v1.1.22 compile exit 0; zero .ak
files touched so the fork baseline holds by construction. Two review
rounds (2 majors + 8 minors, then LAND with 5 prose minors); parent-only
surfaces untouched.

refactor(onchain): rebind Q21 transition-trace onto the authenticated field door (#577)

Phase-5 lane C: the transition-trace family (Q21) now consumes body fields
exclusively through the §8.8 authenticated_field_view door via the #575

open_field_walk call with a hand-rolled unread witness set is gone; both
rebound sites sit behind carriage_reaches_the_anchor and the §2.5 pairing.
Counted-scheme codec twins and the proof-step witness idiom
(verify_native_tx_proof_source_v1 / native_tx_proof_commitment_v1) are
deleted from the claimed directory; the door's §5.4 aggregate byte cap is

were dropped only after proving their value pinned elsewhere (MPF membership
on the L2 side, tx-order NFT reference input on the forced side).

Disjoint single-writer lane: claimed only Q21 transition-trace, disjoint
from #575 (Q1x) and #576 (Q31); claim recorded on the issue before work.

(3,194,009 -> 3,034,025 mem), L2 path +8.9% (2,533,821 -> 2,760,481 mem).
The regression's cause is exact and disclosed - first script in the wave to
open two fields, so the tx id is re-derived three times; the multi-field
opening that fixes it is filed as #584, blocking #579. Neutralisation set
re-derived by mutation: 5 selectors / 4 mutations, each with a distinct red

(exported GOAL_SPEC_EXECUTION_BASIS_V1 constant, zero-row refusal, named
shape errors, 12-case self-test) consumed by the Q21 and migrated Q31
verifiers; q1x/carriage verifiers keep their derived-row shape but now take
the basis from the shared constant and refuse zero-row runs - all guards
negatively probed. All four ledgers get uniform CI pin steps, the two
compile-free self-tests are hoisted above every fallible step, and the
pre-existing normalized-fmt drift is fixed at root cause (9 files from
landed tickets; reformat byte-identical under stock v1.1.22 and fork
v1.1.23+2a78108, fixed point under both, all four ledgers re-verified to
the unit afterwards). Epoch-645 basis provenance corrected in three ledgers
per GOAL_SPEC §3.3.

Fork-runner: family suite 38/38 (+3 new vectors); full check 2301 checks /
34 errors = HEAD's identical failure set, none in transition_trace. Stock
v1.1.22 compiles clean; normalized fmt clean. Survived three review rounds
(1 major + 9 minor, then 3 major + 6 minor, then LAND with 7 pre-existing
or cosmetic minors); parent-only surfaces untouched, deferred exactly to
#584 -> #579.

refactor(onchain): rebind Q31 reference-input-no-idx onto the authenticated field door (#576)

Phase-5 lane B: the reference-input-no-idx family (Q31) now threads the
disputed transaction's id instead of its field commitments, opening field 1
(reference inputs) and field 2 (outputs) through the §10 authenticated_field_view
door via the #575 FieldOpeningV1 idiom. Steps 01→02 thread verified_tx_id and
03→04 thread producing_tx_id; step-02 opens field 1 with spend_input_at (field 1
shares field 0's 38-byte stride), step-04 reads field 2 via field_item_count.
Both are body fields (0-5), so BodyAnchor{tx_id} covers them — the family

feat(onchain): intra-item package — Value bookmark, Canonical-Data Acceptor, native-script pushdown (#571)

The Phase-3b intra-item access package, worked as one unit in the machine
lane, plus §11 written into docs/spec/midgard-tx.md — the section #566
reserved and #570 deliberately did not encroach on.

Case A — Value bookmark (native-tx-intra-item-v1.ak). Ordered intra-item
access into a multiasset value without materialising the output. 64 lookups
over 8 policies x 8 assets cost 12.22M mem against the 13,200,000-mem
GOAL_SPEC §3.3 basis; the materialising control costs 20.15M and does not
fit. The two are pinned to the same 64 answers, so the comparison means
something. The gap decomposes as 6.10M fixed plus 1.83M marginal — recorded
that way rather than as a single headline, because the fixed decode dominates
and `decode_canonical_output` also decides datum and script_ref, which the
bookmark never inspects.

Case B — Canonical-Data Acceptor. Datum interior access at 0.93M and 4.87M,
both far inside the basis. Reported honestly: the `cbor.deserialise` controls
are cheaper (0.18M / 1.07M) with no crossover at width, since deserialise is
a builtin and the acceptor is interpreted. Case B is a capability case, not a
cost case, and §11.4 says so — an earlier "materialisation is priced by the
whole item" claim was removed because the measurement refutes it for datums.

The capability is real, and it closes #567's residual. #567 screened
top-level bignum-headed datums with a head-byte check and documented that
nested bignums — canonical at any depth — still aborted the script, deferring
the fix here. Under PV11 `ConstrData` takes a Word64, and Aiken stdlib's
`cbor.deserialise` computes `ix = tag - 121` with no range guard, so any CBOR
tag below 121 aborts. The recursive acceptor now declines instead, verified
for a bignum as a map key, first-in-list, mid-list, at depth 5, and inside
tag-102. `is_canonical_plutus_data_v1`'s verdict is provably unchanged, so
L1 parity and #567's AC4 hold: canonical and materialisable stay separate
questions.

Case C — native-script checkpointable pushdown. Traversal 1.42M, checkpoint
and resume 1.79M, recursive-checker control 1.26M. The cursor is 87 bytes,
constant across scripts, `pub opaque` with a private decoder and only the
commitment-taking resume exported — #570's §10.6 shape preserved.

Two consensus divergences from the definitional checker, both caught by
review and both fixed
- The depth bound counted frames where `native_script_v1` counts nodes with a
  leaf at depth 1, so the pushdown admitted depth 17 while the checker refused
  it. On 16 nested `all` around one signature the checker returned None and
  the pushdown returned Some(True). Fixed with an explicit
  `max_native_script_frames = max_native_script_depth - 1`, and the agreement
  test now spans depths 1, 2, 15 and 16 rather than stopping at 3, with the
  other side pinned so the fix cannot over-refuse.
- `required` carried an upper bound the definition does not have, so
  `at_least(33, [signature])` — which the checker evaluates to Some(False) —
  aborted instead. A script the definition calls invalid could not be
  adjudicated at all. `required` is now capped rather than bounded: anything
  above the node count maps onto `unsatisfiable_required`, which preserves the
  verdict because `satisfied` can never reach it, while keeping the frame's
  wire scalar three bytes wide.

Guard coverage follows §9.5's discipline. §11.5 enumerates 36 refusals — 29
isolated, 7 backstops — reconciled against the 71 `expect` sites in the new
modules, with every backstop proven by neutralisation rather than argued. The
first recount said 15; auditing found 21 more, including one whose stated
"checked one step earlier" rebuttal was simply false.

Also fixed in review: the cursor's array header spelled `88` over seven
elements, so the wire form was not decodable CBOR — now `87`, with a test
that decodes it; the resume test could not detect a restart-from-zero, now
budgeted at exactly the remaining work and pinned both ways;
`datum_alternative_at_v1` aborted where §11 promises None, now guarded like
its two siblings; and the §5.6 citations for an output-value name cap were
re-pointed to §5.5, which now states the basis it was missing.

Note for future neutralisation work: deleting a guard whose constrained value
has no other consumer makes Aiken erase the whole computation, which reddens
many tests for the wrong reason. Weaken the predicate instead.
